title: Delegation with a Weak Delegate
hints: Delegates are stored `weak` to avoid retain cycles — which needs a class-only protocol.
Declare `protocol DownloaderDelegate: AnyObject`, store `weak var delegate`, and log "dropped" when it's `nil`.
jsBridge: Delegation is Apple's callback pattern: an object holds a `weak var delegate: P?` and calls methods on it. It's like passing an event-handler object in JS, but `weak` is required to avoid retain cycles, and `AnyObject` restricts the protocol to classes.

compass.q: JS event emitters hold strong references to listeners too. Why doesn't that leak in JS (GC handles cycles) but does in Swift (ARC doesn't)?
Delegate vs closure callback vs Combine vs async sequence: which does modern Swift prefer, and when is a delegate still best?
Why must the protocol be `: AnyObject` to be used with `weak`?
`UITableViewDelegate` and `UITextFieldDelegate`: what would the SwiftUI equivalent be?
